title: Scalarisation loss, order reflection and observational collapse
completion_criteria: A theorem/countermodel suite cleanly separates (a) noninjective information collapse, (b) monotone-but-not-order-reflecting scoring, (c) impossibility of an order-reflecting embedding into a linear order for genuinely non-total source orders, and (d) any conditions under which a justified scalar utility is legitimate. The connection to T03/V4-Q1/CV-R is explicitly typed rather than asserted by analogy.

title: Congeniality and admissible common comparison without commensurability
completion_criteria: Supply a nonvacuous definition with examples/counterexamples proving that common admission does not entail equality, total comparability, scalar utility, common policy, or canonical operational licence. Identify any lawful bridge to analysis-relative contexts.

title: Endogenous faculty-mediated observation architecture
completion_criteria: A well-typed architecture and at least one theorem/countermodel establishes a substantive difference between endogenous multi-locus mediation and a flat external-observer encoding, while making no empirical claim about human cognitive anatomy.

title: Mixed-policy semantics and the fixed-point/equilibrium bridge
completion_criteria: Produce a dependency-complete equilibrium theorem statement, with every compactness/convexity/nonempty-value/continuity-or-closed-graph/payoff assumption explicit as applicable, plus a separation between existence, computability, convergence, truth and authority.

title: Solution-concept separation: scalar Nash, vector/Pareto, team, constrained and pipeline models
completion_criteria: A precise decision/assumption matrix and proof/countermodel family shows which additional structures license each solution concept and blocks silent scalarisation. If vector-equilibrium existence needs external theorems, cite exact hypotheses rather than asserting it.

title: L0-L7 assumption/admissibility hierarchy with no-credit-leak countermodels
completion_criteria: Deliver a machine-readable dependency map plus theorem/countermodel explanations that prevent higher-level equilibrium or normative conclusions from receiving lower-level evidence credit.

title: Robustness and invariance under re-encoding
completion_criteria: At least one positive invariance theorem and one sharp counterexample delimit when the application is representation-sensitive. State which conclusions are coordinate-free and which are encoding-dependent.

title: Applied Orthemology specification and proof/countermodel suite for later Codex implementation
completion_criteria: A Codex-ready handoff names exact proposed definitions/theorems/tests, source dependencies, required literature citations, formal pins, negative controls, status labels and rollback/non-goals. It must state whether the PDF contributes a genuine applied theorem/test domain, remains merely analogical, or is partly rejected.
